about: Interactive messages (messages.kind = 'hypertext', docs/HYPERTEXT.md), card format v1: the shared contract of the C++ server (backend/src/chat/Hypertext.cpp, unit_tests), the web app (frontend/src/hypertext), Android (core/Hypertext.kt) and iOS (AcerciaeCore/Hypertext.swift). Change this file first, then every reader. Sections and readers: engine (TS, mobile bundle test, Android, iOS); validation, fallback, templates (C++); dice_policy, defaults, state_validation, conditions, interpolation (C++, TS, Kotlin, Swift). Later phases add bindings, resolve, act (TS, Kotlin, Swift) and runs (TS engine, node:vm bundle, iOS simulator), each a list of {name, ...} cases like the others. validation: input {hypertext, replies?} is a post body; ok:true cases may pin normalized (the card with defaults filled in), private (the stored reply templates) and public (messages.hypertext for public.closes_at); ok:false cases give error_path, the path of the first error in the post body (hypertext.body[0].label, replies.r.text). fallback: text is the content posted when a card (with its replies, if any) has none. templates: reply is one posted reply, slots what a client sends; text, or error invalid_slot; allow_dice as stored. dice_policy: verdict of a line posted as the clicker (allowed | confirm | refused | none). defaults: state_decl is a card's state, state its default state. state_validation: error is the offending key, "" for the whole state. conditions: evalCondition(cond) over state_decl and state. interpolation: interpolate(text) over the hypertext and state. Interpolated ({{key}}): text nodes, the labels of checkbox, choice, input and button, group titles and act.say; the card title, placeholders, submit labels and value labels are literal. Condition depth counts every level, the leaf included (all > any > leaf is 3 deep), at most 8 leaves per show_if or enable_if. Lengths count code points. Numbers are integers within ±1e9 (1.0 equals 1). Bidi, control and noncharacter cases are written as \u escapes; lone surrogates and invalid UTF-8 cannot be written portably in JSON, so each reader tests those itself.
